external.label: Bulk silica and mineral proportions — USGS
external.citation: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, Components of Igneous Rocks
external.supports: An illustrative granite composition distinguishes bulk SiO₂ from mineral proportions. It is not an Egyptian sample.
external.access: Full page and indexed description

external.label: Giza stone supply — Mark Lehner
external.citation: Mark Lehner, The Treasures of the Pyramids, pp. 32–45
external.supports: Archaeological description of local core limestone, imported fine casing limestone and Aswan granite. Supply description is not a specimen assay.
external.access: Indexed primary-author PDF

external.label: Pyramid petrography — Campbell and Folk, 1991
external.citation: D. H. Campbell and R. L. Folk, Ancient Egyptian Pyramids—Concrete or Rock, Concrete International 13(8), 28, 30–39 (1991)
external.supports: Reports geological fabrics and absence of proposed geopolymer fabric in examined material. Preserve sample scope.
external.access: Publisher abstract; full paper not inspected

external.label: Granite and molten carbonate — Yi, 2026
external.citation: Xiang Yi, npj Heritage Science 14, 51 (2026), published 22 January 2026
external.supports: Modern thermal/carbonate experiments; short-contact cracking is attributed mainly to thermal shock. Does not establish a Khufu manufacturing history.
external.access: Publisher-indexed Methods, Results and Discussion; direct page retrieval redirected to an inaccessible identity endpoint

external.label: Reaction interfaces — Winter et al., 2005
external.citation: R. Winter et al., Tracing the reactive melting of glass-forming silicate batches by in situ 23Na NMR, DOI 10.1021/jp045705s
external.supports: Primary powder-batch NMR evidence for metasilicate formation and changing interface-controlled kinetics. Massive-rock scaling requires additional inputs.
external.access: Primary research abstract indexed in PubMed; publisher full text inaccessible

external.label: Aqueous quartz kinetics — Worley et al., 1996
external.citation: W. G. Worley, J. W. Tester and C. O. Grigsby, AIChE Journal 42, 3442–3457 (1996)
external.supports: Aqueous 100–200 °C quartz kinetics; apparent activation energy 72 ± 6 kJ/mol in the stated NaOH/NaCl regime. No molten-salt extrapolation.
external.access: Publisher abstract and indexed original paper at https://electronicsandbooks.com/edt/manual/Magazine/A/AIChE%20Journal%20US/1996%20v.42/12%20%283301-3570%29/3442-3457.pdf

external.label: Firesetting field evidence — Storemyr, 2014
external.citation: Per Storemyr, field-author account of Heldal et al., DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-09048-1_56
external.supports: Quarry-context observations and experiments provide thermal/mechanical comparators. Their site and date do not transfer automatically to Khufu.
external.access: Full author account; linked chapter not independently reanalysed

external.label: Natron composition — Raman study, 2007
external.citation: Raman spectroscopy of natron: shedding light on ancient Egyptian mummification (2007)
external.supports: Natural deposits contain carbonate, bicarbonate and chloride/sulfate impurities; composition must be specified rather than equated with a hydroxide reagent.
external.access: Primary research abstract

external.label: Carbonate formula mass — NIST WebBook
external.citation: NIST Chemistry WebBook, sodium carbonate
external.supports: Na₂CO₃ molecular weight 105.9884; reference for the rounded formula-mass arithmetic. Other formula masses are declared calculation constants.
external.access: Indexed reference entry

external.label: Confounding and experimental design — NIST
external.citation: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 5.3.3.4.3 Confounding (also called aliasing)
external.supports: Explains that confounded design terms cannot be estimated separately. Method reference; supplies no granite responses or productivity measurements.
external.access: Public handbook section and related indexed factorial/blocking guidance

external.label: Reconstitution interpretation — Barsoum et al., 2006
external.citation: M. W. Barsoum, A. Ganguly and G. Hug, Journal of the American Ceramic Society 89(12), 3788–3796 (2006)
external.supports: Microscopy-based reconstitution argument; specimen and binder interpretations must retain their particular scope.
external.access: Full primary paper read from a public mirror; Table I specimen listing checked in extracted text; canonical metadata checked against Drexel repository.

external.label: Spatial petrographic counterargument — Jana, 2007
external.citation: Dipayan Jana, The Great Pyramid Debate, Proceedings of the 29th Conference on Cement Microscopy (2007), pp. 207–266
external.supports: Natural-stone/alteration interpretation and located EDS entries; Figure 15 attributes earlier Harrell material.
external.access: Primary full PDF reviewed selectively: specimen descriptions, comparison arguments and Figure 15; figure rendered locally for visual transcription. Raw spectra not available in this audit.

external.label: Lauer natural-limestone interpretation — Harrell and Penrod, 1993
external.citation: J. A. Harrell and B. E. Penrod, Journal of Geological Education 41(4), 358–363 (1993)
external.supports: Publisher abstract concludes that the examined Lauer sample is natural limestone.
external.access: Publisher-indexed abstract inspected; full original paper unavailable here. Figure/data attributed to Harrell in Jana is not treated as full-text access to this paper.

external.label: Hydrothermal granite mass-loss rate — Hillson and Tester, 2015
external.citation: S. D. Hillson and J. W. Tester, Heat Transfer Properties and Dissolution Behavior of Barre Granite as Applied to Hydrothermal Jet Drilling with Chemical Enhancement, Stanford Geothermal Workshop, SGP-TR-204 (2015)
external.supports: Bulk mass-loss range and operating context; geometric-area definition in Section 4.2, Eq. 4.
external.access: Primary PDF abstract and Sections 4.1–4.2 read; abstract rendered for visual check. No matched raw trial series extracted.

external.label: Granite residue composition — Cui et al., 2022
external.citation: Z. Cui et al., Experimental Study on the Effect and Mechanism of Chemical Stimulation on Deep High-Temperature Granite, Frontiers in Earth Science 10, 893969 (2022)
external.supports: Static powder treatment context and Table 3 normalized phase compositions. No absolute phase loss inferred from percentages alone.
external.access: Primary full article and PDF methods/table read; Table 3, PDF p. 9, rendered and visually checked. Dashes retained; quantitative mass basis and paired residue yield not established for the selected transcription.

external.label: Hydrothermal spallation and partition limits — Beentjes et al., 2018
external.citation: I. Beentjes, J. T. Bender, S. D. Hillson and J. W. Tester, Hydrothermal Spallation Of Barre Granite Using Supercritical Water Jets, Stanford Geothermal Workshop, SGP-TR-213 (2018)
external.supports: Coupled alteration, particulate removal and precipitation motivate separate stream measurements.
external.access: Primary PDF, especially Section 6, reviewed selectively. Diluted-effluent concentrations not measured; no numerical conditions extracted for the comparison.

external.label: Casing-base survey — Dash, 2015
external.citation: Glen Dash, AERAGRAM 16-2 (Fall 2015), Great Pyramid survey report, printed pp.8–14
external.supports: Casing-base side estimates; platform distinguished from casing.
external.access: Primary PDF Table 1, printed p.11, locally rendered and visually checked. Selected survey discussion read; covariance not reconstructed.

external.label: Stone transport logbook — Tallet, 2017
external.citation: Pierre Tallet, Les papyrus de la mer Rouge I, English annex translated by Colin Clement (2017), pp.149–152
external.supports: Located transport entries and author interpretation, with textual lacunae and limits.
external.access: Primary English translation, Papyrus B I and summary, read. No whole-project payload or rate inferred.

external.label: Wet and dry sand friction — Fall et al., 2014
external.citation: Fall et al., Physical Review Letters 112, 175502 (2014), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.112.175502
external.supports: Sand-dependent laboratory friction change and capillary/elastic response.
external.access: Primary published paper in university repository, methods and Figure 5 discussion read. No ancient coefficient or route identified.

external.label: Stone drilling experiments — Gorelick and Gwinnett, 1983
external.citation: Leonard Gorelick and A. John Gwinnett, Ancient Egyptian Stone-Drilling, Expedition (1983)
external.supports: Preliminary object-specific replication and competing abrasive explanations.
external.access: Primary museum article read, including conclusions. Its object-specific interpretation is not promoted to every pyramid operation; erroneous chemical description of corundum is not adopted.

external.label: Giza field recording — AERA/ISAC, 2024–25
external.citation: Giza Plateau Mapping Project, ISAC Annual Report 2024–2025
external.supports: Reported survey recording of worked platform features.
external.access: Primary project report indexed passage inspected; no raw point cloud or productivity series obtained.

external.label: Pyramid dating and inbuilt age — AERA
external.citation: AERA, How Old Are the Pyramids? project account
external.supports: Organic-material dating, calibration and older-material interpretations require event association.
external.access: Primary project account read; no dates recalibrated or new chronological posterior calculated.

external.label: Provisioning and fuel — AERA
external.citation: AERA, Feeding Pyramid Workers
external.supports: Settlement provisioning and fuel belong in the construction system.
external.access: Primary project synthesis inspected; food/fuel quantities not extracted as a calibrated full-project inventory.

external.citation: US General Services Administration, Life cycle assessment and buildings
external.supports: Functional unit, whole-building coverage and service-life comparison.
external.access: Official methodological guidance read; supplies none of the illustrative Australian cost or emissions factors.

external.citation: WA Building and Energy, Industry Bulletin 176 (May 2026)
external.supports: NCC 2025 adoption from 1 May 2026 and specific WA modifications.
external.access: Official bulletin read; not a complete project-specific compliance assessment or licensed full standards text.

external.citation: WA Building and Energy, Industry Bulletin 173 (April 2026)
external.supports: PCA 2025 and referenced AS/NZS 3500 Parts 1,2,4:2025, with WA variations.

external.citation: WA Building and Energy, Electrical technical guidance

external.access: Official current guidance inspected; no circuit design or electrical compliance certification performed.

external.citation: Bureau of Meteorology, station 009225, Perth Metro
external.supports: Station climatology distinguishes seasonal temperature and rainfall inputs.
external.access: Official monthly statistics inspected 30 October 2026. Climate averages are not site wind, bushfire, flood or drainage design values.

external.citation: S. Hemeda and A. Sonbol, Sustainability problems of the Giza pyramids, Heritage Science 8,8 (2020)
external.supports: Mortar grouping and selected Table 17 aggregate entries.
external.access: Primary paper read from a public PDF mirror; Table 17 rendered and visually checked. No new specimen custody or joint chronology established.
